items.evidence: play --ticks 5 printed one JSON object, screen title, with all 23 keys of the brief (tick, screen, menu_index, volume, difficulty, texts, cursor, piece, stock, grid, slot, slots, clock, speed, coins, served, lost, queue, customers, arrivals, replaying, replay_ready, ledger).
play ... --frame f_*.png --size 800x480 wrote PNGs; `file` reports 800 x 480 RGBA for all 9 frames taken (title, settings, ledger x2, layout, night x2, paused, summary, replay).
Fresh: texts [Night Market, Layout, Ledger, Settings, Quit], menu_index 0; down x6 -> 1,2,3,3,3; up x5 -> back to 0 and stays 0.
Settings: Volume: 5 / Difficulty: Normal at first; left x7 -> 0 and stays; right x12 -> 10 and stays; on Difficulty right -> Hard (stays), left -> Normal, Easy (stays); escape -> title.
Run 1 with --settings s2 set volume 3, hard; run 2 with s2 opened Settings showing Volume: 3, Difficulty: Hard; new folder s3 showed 5 / Normal.
1:enter -> layout, cursor (0,0), piece stove, slot 1, stock 3/4/2, grid [], texts Layout, Piece: Stove, Slot: 1, Stove: 3, Table: 4, Lamp: 2 plus Enter/Escape lines.

With a none between words the cursor moves one cell a word, up raises y, stops at x 0/7 and y 0/4, menu_index stays null, screen stays layout. But the same word given twice in a script without a none between (2:right,3:right,4:right, or every 2 ticks 25:right..41:right, 11:up..19:up) moves only one cell: not one cell for each Up/Down/Left/Right.
next_piece x3: table, lamp, stove; prev_piece x3: lamp, table, stove; texts Piece: Table / Lamp / Stove followed (words separated by none).
place on (0,0) stove 3->2; place again on occupied (0,0) no change; 3 stoves then 4th refused (stock 0, grid unchanged); 4 tables then 5th at (7,1) refused; 2 lamps then 3rd at (7,4) refused.
erase on empty (7,4) changed nothing; erase lamp at (7,3): grid lost it, stock lamp 0->1, text Lamp: 1.
Cursor moved to (2,0), escape -> title, enter -> layout with cursor (0,0) and same grid; a later run with the same --settings folder s7 showed the same grid.
next_slot 1->2->3->1; save_slot filled slot 1 / slot 2 and left grid as it was; load_slot on empty slot 3 changed nothing; load_slot slot 1 replaced grid (table removed, stock table 3->4).
Second run on s7 showed the same three slots; next_slot, load_slot gave grid stove(0,0)+table(1,0) as saved in slot 2.

Enter with empty grid and with a stove only: screen layout, texts gain "Needs a stove and a table" (gone after the next word); with stove+table: screen night, clock 0, speed slow, coins/served/lost 0, grid unchanged, 18:00.

Night started tick 12: clock 1 at tick 36, 2 at 60 (24 ticks); fast at 70 -> clock 3 at 74, 4 at 80 (progress kept); stop at 80: clock 4 to tick 221, screen night; slow at 200 -> clock 5 at 222 (progress 2 kept). Texts 18:0N and Speed: Slow/Fast/Stop followed.
Seed 1 arrivals [5,12,18,23,33,...,350,356], gaps all 4..10, last under 360, identical across runs and at every tick of the night; seeds 4, 9, 10 gave other lists.
Tables (2,1),(2,4),(3,1): customers 1,2,3 sat at (2,1),(2,4),(3,1); with one table customers queued with x/y null; with queue 3, arrival at 33 turned away and lost 0->1 at that minute.
Stove (0,0) + table (1,0): c1 cooking at 5, eating at 25. Stove (0,0) + table (2,0): cooking at 5, eating at 35.
Adjacent case: at 35 c1 gone, served 1, coins 8, table taken by next; with a lamp at (2,0) next to table (1,0): coins 12 at 35.
Hard, non-adjacent: c1 still cooking at 34, gone at 35 with coins 0, lost +1, stove at once cooking c2. Normal: c2 (arr 12) left at 52 (wait 40). Easy: c2 (arr 12) cooking at 71 wait 59, gone at 72.
At 35 c1 paid and c2 (queued) was seated and cooking in the same minute; at 52 c2 left and c3 moved from the queue to the table and began cooking at 52.
Slow night: tick 8651 screen summary, clock 360, texts Night over, Coins: 24, Served: 3, Lost: 49, Enter: title; lost 49 at 359 too, although 4 customers were still in the stall; Enter -> title.
Same grid, seed 1, Normal: slow 24/3/49; fast 24/3/49; fast-stop-slow-fast-stop-fast-slow-fast 24/3/49.

Escape -> paused, texts Paused, Resume, Title, clock stood at 4 for 30 ticks; Resume (enter) and Escape both returned to night with the same clock and its progress; Title -> title, ledger unchanged, Replay still played the earlier seed-1 night.
After the night, ledger [{24,3,49,normal}]; a later run on s6 showed it and the Ledger screen read "Coins 24, served 3, lost 49, Normal"; fresh place: "No nights yet".
On s6b 4 finished nights (seeds 1,2,3,4) plus a replay and a given-up night: ledger 56/7/44, 8/1/45, 24/3/41 (newest first, the first night gone).
After the night the title read Layout, Replay, Ledger, Settings, Quit, replay_ready true, also in a later run on the same folder.

Replay run with seed 7, Hard and another grid: night, replaying true, "Replay", seed-1 arrivals, Replay over 24/3/49, ledger and kept night unchanged; the frame draws the kept grid. But the state's grid key during the replay is the current editor grid (table(1,1), stove(2,1)), not the night's grid, while customers sit at (1,0).
After changing the grid, saving it to slot 1, erasing, load_slot, and setting Hard, Replay still gave the seed-1 arrivals and 24/3/49 with customers at the old table (1,0).
Two copies of the same kept folder, seed 9, same 900-tick script (pause, stop, fast): full outputs byte-identical (cmp); seed 10 gave other arrivals.

f_layout.png: 8x5 grid, stove red, table brown, lamp yellow at (0,0),(1,0),(2,0), blue cursor at (4,2) holding a small lamp-colour square, panel Piece: Lamp, Slot: 2, Stove: 2, Table: 3, Lamp: 1, as in the state.

f_night.png / f_night_seated.png: grid and pieces, queued customer as a grey-blue square at the left, seated pale yellow, cooking orange, eating green on their tables, panel Coins, Served, Lost, 18:26, Speed: Slow.
Frames of title, settings, ledger (empty and 3 lines), paused and summary show their texts, and the chosen entry has a focus ring (Ledger, Difficulty, Title); the summary has no menu.

README has keys/how to play, says what is kept in --settings FOLDER/settings.json (kept.k_* entries, confirmed in the file), and its play and --frame commands ran as written (summary 24/3/49; 800x480 PNG).

defects: The headless run does not honour 'each acts once, even when the same word was given at the tick before': a Layout/Night word (right, up, place, enter, ...) repeated in a script counts once unless a none is put between, even when 2 or more ticks apart (README admits it). Enter in Layout right after the title's Enter is also ignored without a none between.
A word at tick 0 does nothing (0:enter leaves the title); the state at tick 0 has screen null.
Quit in a headless run does not end the run: the printed tick is the full --ticks count (30), not the tick of Quit.
During a replay the state's grid key shows the editor grid, not the grid being replayed.
On the title and paused screens the first button is always drawn filled blue (primary style) while the focus ring is elsewhere, so two entries look marked.

trace.how: context, new, read_again and how far the context grew are the run's own records. written_out a request is its growth less its answers (characters / 4), scaled to the run's exact total; of_which_unseen is that less the visible text (thinking). cost is what the request read and wrote, weighted; carried is what reading again what it added cost at every later request (start.carried: the same for what every request starts from). reading + writing is in_the_ledger
